name: Jane Street
summary: Jane Street describes a video technical interview followed by in-person final rounds of collaborative coding. Candidates report open-ended, multi-part implementation problems (games, data structures, small interpreters) that grow as the interviewer adds requirements, rather than puzzle or math questions.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.what: Background, interest in Jane Street and what you want next.

rounds.name: Technical screen
rounds.what: One multi-part coding problem over video in a real language; reasoning and communication count more than reaching the optimum.

rounds.name: Onsite coding rounds
rounds.what: Several collaborative rounds in CoderPad on underspecified problems you build out from scratch and extend.

rounds.name: Project deep dive
rounds.what: Present a technically complex past project and field detailed follow-ups; reported for mid to senior candidates.

tips: Use the language you know best; Jane Street says OCaml earns no extra credit.
Write real code, not pseudocode, and know your language's basic data structure APIs.
Say what you do not know instead of guessing, and agree on a plan before changing course.
SWE interviews do not include mental math or logic puzzles, so practise building things instead.
If you recognise a question, tell the interviewer so they can switch it.

reported.note: Jane Street's own published example: memoize a function, then add FIFO and LRU eviction
